classification.difficultyReason: Use the composite logarithmic derivative to form tangent and normal equations, then use the explicitly requested intercepts and a sketch to identify the triangle's base and perpendicular height.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the point $P(1,0)$ lies on the curve $y=\ln(3x-2)$.

answer.short: At $x=1$, $y=\ln 1=0$, so $P(1,0)$ lies on the curve.
answer.worked:
When $x=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\ln(3(1)-2)\\y&=\ln 1\\y&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $P(1,0)$ lies on the curve.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the equations of the tangent and normal at $P$, and their $y$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{3}{3x-2}\\m_{\text{tangent}}&=\frac{3}{3(1)-2}\\m_{\text{tangent}}&=3.\end{aligned}$$
The tangent passes through $P(1,0)$:
$$\begin{aligned}y-0&=3(x-1)\\y&=3x-3.\end{aligned}$$
Its $y$-intercept is $-3$.
The normal has gradient $-\frac13$:
$$\begin{aligned}y-0&=-\frac13(x-1)\\y&=-\frac13x+\frac13.\end{aligned}$$
Its $y$-intercept is $\frac13$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Sketch the situation and find the area of the triangle formed by the tangent, the normal and the $y$-axis.

answer.worked:
The vertical base joins the $y$-intercepts $-3$ and $\frac13$. The perpendicular height is the horizontal distance from $P(1,0)$ to the $y$-axis.
$$\begin{aligned}b&=\frac13-(-3)=\frac{10}{3}\\h&=1\\A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{(\frac13+3)(1)}{2}\\A&=\frac53\text{ square units}.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Equation-driven logarithmic curve, dashed vertical asymptote, tangent and normal, with the two source-labelled y-intercepts. Axes use house black; semantic series use the standard palette.
spec.mathematics: Curve y=ln(3x-2), asymptote x=2/3, tangent y=3x-3 and normal y=-x/3+1/3 intersect at (1,0). The y-intercepts are -3 and 1/3.
